REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MAY 11, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Sierra Room.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, MAY
11, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE SIERRA ROOM AT CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING
ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the 2023 BASES program – Leal Elementary School.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Cerritos High School Model United Nations Team (Award of Distinction – Debate; Award of
  Distinction – Research and Preparation).

  REQUEST FOR REORDERING OF THE AGENDA

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, requested City Council consensus, pursuant to the provisions of
  Section 8.09 of the City Council Protocol Manual, to reorder the agenda in order to consider
  Closed Session Items 12B, 12C, and 12D (described below) at this juncture of the meeting.
  He noted the City Attorney’s Office received information concerning material all
  Councilmembers recently received related to public employee evaluations. He affirmed the
  City Council should review the relevant information in Closed Session prior to consideration
  of Open Session agenda items.

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, the agenda was reordered to consider Closed Session
  Items 12B, 12C, and 12D at this juncture of the meeting.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for Items 12B, 12C, and 12D. Noting there
  were no individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Bob Quinlan spoke regarding the Neighborhood Watch Program, corruption in local
  governments, City Council meeting videos on the City’s website, and the “If you see
  something, say something” campaign.

  Al Barlevy expressed concern regarding conduct and decorum at the previous City Council
  meeting and expressed opposition to the previous adoption of an ordinance changing the
  date of the Cerritos General Municipal Election.

  Jay Gray spoke expressed concern regarding City Council stipends, term limits, and the
  City Treasurer appointment.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the 2023 Let Freedom Ring
  Celebration – 50th anniversary event (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherré Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to receive and file this report
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration by the City Council of the City of Cerritos of the financial status of
  the water and sewer utility enterprise funds, and discussion of options, including possible
  future rate adjustments, to address ongoing operational and maintenance costs of the
  referenced utilities (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Jay Gray inquired of water and sewer enterprise loans and spoke in opposition to water and
  sewer utility rate increases.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted written
  correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  The following individuals submitted comments in opposition to water and sewer utility rate
  increases:

  Marty and Gail Grossman
  Bev Brown
  Ruth and Ron Leopold
  Maria and Amos Garcia
  Murali Vasudevan
  Charles Murphy
  Adriana Timoney
  Kanchan Premjani
  Rostam Namiranian
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 11, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 9

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to provide a
  report to the City Council on 1. The feasibility of negotiating a transfer of Cerritos sewer utility
  infrastructure maintenance and billing liability to the Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts 2,
  3, 18, and 19; and 2. The feasibility of creating a similar sewer infrastructure maintenance and
  billing system as the City of Lakewood and other surrounding cities whose systems are operated
  by the Los Angeles County Sanitation District (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  Johnson
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to write off the
  outstanding loan balances of the water and sewer fund in a lump sum (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager, on a request by the
  League of California Cities (Cal Cities) for support for action needed to address Fentanyl
  and other substance use-related legislation.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to prepare a
  letter endorsed by the City Council in support of Assembly Bill (AB) 474 (Rodriguez), AB 33
  (Bains), and AB 701 (Villapudua) and send the letter on Friday, May 12, 2023 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Items 12B, 12C, and 12D although provided earlier in the meeting and memorialized in

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council convened into Closed Session to
